headline: Hurricane Polo Threatens Northwest Mexico with Life-Threatening Flooding as Tropical Moisture Triggers Widespread US Southwest Flood Watches
overview: A cluster of simultaneous natural disasters is unfolding across multiple continents on September 27, 2026. In the Pacific, Hurricane Polo is bearing down on Mexico's Baja Peninsula and Sonora with landfall expected Monday, while its moisture drives flood watches across Arizona, New Mexico, Colorado, and Texas. Simultaneously, Anak Krakatau's ongoing eruptive sequence has produced a remarkable geological development — two entirely new islands detected in the Sunda Strait — and a powerful Nor'easter continues to batter the US East Coast with up to 3 feet of coastal inundation from Virginia to Massachusetts.

events.title: Hurricane Polo — Category 5 Storm Threatens Northwest Mexico, Flood Watches Blanket US Southwest
events.location: Baja Peninsula, Sinaloa, Sonora, Mexico; Arizona, New Mexico, Colorado, Texas, USA
events.summary: Hurricane Polo, which rapidly intensified to Category 5 status earlier in the week, is now on a track to impact northern coastal Sinaloa, the Baja Peninsula, and the Sonora coast from late Monday, September 28, through Tuesday, with heavy rain, flooding, mudslides, and road closures expected. Tropical moisture streaming northward ahead of the storm has prompted Flood Watches across large portions of Arizona, New Mexico, Colorado, and far west Texas, with NWS El Paso explicitly citing Hurricane Polo as the moisture source. The storm poses a life-threatening flooding risk on both sides of the US–Mexico border, making it the most consequential weather system globally today.

events.title: Nor'easter Coastal Flooding Persists — Up to 3 Feet of Inundation, Gale-Force Gusts Across Northeast US
events.location: Virginia to Massachusetts, US East Coast
events.summary: The stalled Nor'easter continues to hammer the US East Coast on September 27, with active Coastal Flood Warnings spanning from Virginia Beach and the Outer Banks through New Jersey, New York City, Long Island, Connecticut, and into Massachusetts, with inundation levels of 2–3 feet above ground reported in the most vulnerable areas. High Wind Warnings remain active across coastal New Jersey, Long Island, and Connecticut, with gusts reaching 50–60 mph, accompanied by surf of 7–15 feet and dangerous rip currents. New York City (46.9 mm precipitation) reflects the storm's continued intensity, with the broader warning footprint representing one of the most extensive Northeast coastal flood events in recent years.

events.title: Anak Krakatau Eruptions Form Two New Islands in Sunda Strait
events.summary: Indonesia's Geological Agency has detected two entirely new islands that have formed northwest and southeast of Anak Krakatau in the Sunda Strait, a dramatic geological development resulting from the volcano's intense and sustained eruptive sequence that included an ash column reaching 50,000 feet earlier this week. The new landmasses — confirmed by the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources — represent a significant reshaping of the Sunda Strait and indicate the eruption has deposited substantial new volcanic material above sea level. The volcano remains at high alert, and maritime and aviation exclusion zones are expected to remain in place.

events.title: Bangkok Flooding Ongoing — Thousands Displaced as Rain Eases Across Thailand
events.summary: Although rainfall has begun to ease across parts of central Thailand, persistent floodwaters continue to force thousands of residents from their homes in Bangkok and surrounding provinces as of September 27, with streets still inundated and evacuation efforts ongoing. Meteorological data confirms Bangkok received 36.3 mm of precipitation over the reporting period, maintaining waterlogged conditions across low-lying urban areas. The slow recession of floodwaters, combined with continued high soil saturation across the broader river basin, means the humanitarian impact is expected to persist for several more days.

events.title: Krasheninnikov Volcano Erupts for First Time in 500 Years — Captured by NASA-ISRO NISAR Satellite
events.summary: Russia's Krasheninnikov volcano on the Kamchatka Peninsula has erupted for the first time in approximately 500 years, a highly significant geological event being closely tracked by the joint NASA-ISRO NISAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite, which has captured time-lapse imagery of the eruption and lava flow progression. NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory is leading the US role in the satellite monitoring effort, with India Today reporting that NISAR has successfully imaged the newly extruded lava. The reactivation of a centuries-dormant volcano on one of the world's most volcanically active peninsulas is being closely watched by volcanologists for its potential to escalate.

events.title: Hurricane Nolo Exits Hawaii — Damaging Winds and Flash Flood Threat Linger Through Sunday
events.location: Hawaiʻi Island, Maui, Lanai, Molokai, Hawaii, USA
events.summary: Hurricane Nolo has moved south-southwest of the Big Island and is accelerating westward, but active High Wind Warnings covering Maui, Molokai, Lanai, and the Big Island's south and leeward zones remain in effect through 6 PM HST Sunday, with east winds of 30–45 mph and gusts reaching 75 mph still possible over terrain. A Flood Watch covering the entire Big Island was issued through late Sunday night, as moisture from the departing storm continues to threaten flash flooding on flood-prone roads and low-lying areas. Though the worst has likely passed, this remains the third hurricane watch issued for Hawaii in 2026, an unprecedented statistic for the state.

events.title: Galicia Wildfire Burns 460+ Hectares in Ourense — Largest Fire in Spain This Year
events.summary: A major wildfire that ignited on September 24 in the parish of Randin, Calvos de Randin, in Ourense province, Galicia, has spread to over 460 hectares by September 27, making it the largest wildfire recorded in Spain so far in 2026. Crews are battling the fire across steep, difficult terrain in northwestern Spain, with the blaze threatening nearby homes and communities. Aerial and ground resources have been deployed, and the rugged topography of Galicia is hampering containment efforts.
